articles.title: 2026 Node.js Summarize Text API Chat Completions Example for Support Answers
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for a support agent answering from a private knowledge base, the difficult part is not producing a shorter paragraph. It is producing a valid, bounded answer that preserves the facts the…
articles.body: Short answer: for a support agent answering from a private knowledge base, the difficult part is not producing a shorter paragraph. It is producing a valid, bounded answer that preserves the facts the agent is allowed to use. Put that contract in the prompt and application validation, call a chat-completions endpoint, use a temperature around 0.3 to 0.5, and reject output that cannot be parsed. For basic summarization, gpt-4o-mini is a reasonable starting point. A summary that drops a refund restriction is a data-layer defect wearing a language-model costume. How should a Node.js text summarization API use chat completions?

articles.title: How ATS Parsers Read Work Experience Dates, Career Gaps & Overlapping Roles (Greenhouse, Workday & iCIMS Breakdown)
articles.excerpt: When a software engineer or product manager with seven years of full-time experience gets auto-rejected within 90 seconds of applying for a role requiring "5+ years of experience," the culprit is rare…
articles.body: When a software engineer or product manager with seven years of full-time experience gets auto-rejected within 90 seconds of applying for a role requiring "5+ years of experience," the culprit is rarely their skill set. In our audits at Smart Resume Analyzer , date-span tokenization failure is the single most common reason an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) miscalculates total Years of Experience (YoE). Modern hiring platforms—including Workday , Greenhouse , iCIMS , Lever , and Oracle Taleo —do not read work history the way a human recruiter does. Before a recruiter sees your file, an extraction engine ( Textkernel , Sovren , DaXtra , or HireAbility ) converts your layout into a structured HR-XML or JSON payload.

articles.title: How to Stop Claude From Sounding Like AI (My Claude Project Instructions)
articles.excerpt: Every time I opened a new chat in Claude, I used to waste the first ten minutes fixing the exact same problem. I would explain what I do, tell it who I was writing for, and ask for a normal, conversat…
articles.body: Every time I opened a new chat in Claude, I used to waste the first ten minutes fixing the exact same problem. I would explain what I do, tell it who I was writing for, and ask for a normal, conversational tone. Five seconds later, it still handed me stiff paragraphs packed with words nobody says in real life, like "delve," "tapestry," "game-changer," and "in today's fast-paced world." Then I spent twenty minutes rewriting the whole draft by hand. If you want to make Claude write like a human on the first pass, better one-line prompts are not the answer. Putting two short files inside your Claude Project instructions (or your Claude Cowork folder) fixes it permanently. Why Claude sounds stiff out of the box By default, Claude knows nothing about your work, your customers, or how you talk.

articles.excerpt: Taming SQLAlchemy Implicit Flushes: Mitigating Unexpected Deadlocks and Serialization Failures Under High Concurrency Database deadlocks in high-throughput applications are rarely the result of overt…
articles.body: Taming SQLAlchemy Implicit Flushes: Mitigating Unexpected Deadlocks and Serialization Failures Under High Concurrency Database deadlocks in high-throughput applications are rarely the result of overt logic errors. In many Python services built on SQLAlchemy, they stem from an ergonomic feature operating silently in the background: implicit autoflush . When building high-concurrency microservices, developers often focus on choosing between optimistic locking (version checking) and pessimistic locking ( SELECT ... FOR UPDATE ).

articles.body: 전 세계 금융 지형이 깊이 있는 디지털 전환을 겪고 있으며, 이는 돈과 가치 이전의 전통적인 개념에 도전장을 내밀고 있다. 이러한 진화의 최전선에는 중앙은행 디지털 화폐(CBDC)와 암호화폐라는 두 가지 뚜렷하지만 종종 혼동되는 혁신이 자리한다. 둘 다 가치 교환을 위해 디지털 기술을 활용하지만, 그 근본적인 철학, 아키텍처, 목표는 상당히 다르다. 분산화와 검열 저항에 대한 열망에서 탄생한 암호화폐는 주권 화폐에 대한 허가 없는, 종종 가명의 대안을 제시한다. 반대로 CBDC는 중앙집중식의 국가 지원을 받는 법정 화폐의 디지털 형태로, 결제 시스템을 현대화하고, 금융 안정성을 강화하며, 통화 정책의 효율성을 높이는 것을 목표로 한다. 지배적인 서사는 종종 이 두 세력을 서로 대립시켜 디지털 영역에서 지배권을 놓고 피할 수 없는 경쟁을 벌일 것이라고 말한다. 그러나 이러한 단순한 관점은 현재 금융 생태계를 특징짓는 기술적 역량, 진화하는 규제 환경, 다양한 사용 사례의 복잡한 상호작용을 간과한다. 이 글은 전면적인 충돌보다는 CBDC와 암호화폐 간의 미묘한 공존이 디지털 금융의 미래를 더욱 특징지을 것이라고 주장한다. 이 공존은 반드시 완전한 통합을 의미하지는 않는다. 오히려 병렬 시스템, 상호운용 가능한 구성 요소, 그리고 전문화된 애플리케이션의 모자이크 형태가 될 것이다. 각각은 더 넓은 디지털 기반 금융 인프라 내에서 고유한 목적을 수행할 것이다.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.
